title: Total salary
prompt: Show the total of all salaries, as total_pay. Replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT SUM(salary) AS total_pay FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(salary) AS total_pay FROM employees;
SELECT MAX(salary) AS total_pay FROM employees;

title: Price range
prompt: Show the cheapest price as lowest and the highest price as highest.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM books; INSERT INTO books VALUES (10, 'Copper Moon', 'Ada Hill', 'Fantasy', 20.0, 100, 2020), (11, 'North Light', 'Raj Dev', 'Travel', 7.5, 180, 2015), (12, 'Sky Atlas', 'Ada Hill', 'Science', 25.0, 300, 2023);

solutions: SELECT MIN(price) AS lowest, MAX(price) AS highest FROM books;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT MAX(price) AS lowest, MIN(price) AS highest FROM books;
SELECT MIN(price) AS lowest FROM books;

title: Average grade
prompt: Show the average grade, rounded to 2 decimals, as average_grade. NULL grades don't count.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: SELECT ROUND(AVG(grade), 2) AS average_grade FROM enrolments;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(grade) / COUNT(*), 2) AS average_grade FROM enrolments;
wrongSolutions.why: Divides by every row, using integer division

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT AVG(grade) AS average_grade FROM enrolments;

title: Earliest and latest hire
prompt: Show the earliest hire_date as first_hire and the latest as last_hire.
hints: MIN and MAX work on dates in this format.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT MIN(hire_date) AS first_hire, MAX(hire_date) AS last_hire FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT MAX(hire_date) AS first_hire, MIN(hire_date) AS last_hire FROM employees;
SELECT MIN(hire_date) AS first_hire FROM employees;

title: Average with missing values
prompt: Bonuses can be missing. Show the average bonus counting only recorded bonuses as known_avg, and treating missing as 0 as overall_avg, both rounded to 2 decimals.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT ROUND(AVG(bonus), 2) AS known_avg, ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(bonus, 0)), 2) AS overall_avg FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(bonus), 2) AS known_avg, ROUND(AVG(bonus), 2) AS overall_avg FROM employees;
SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(bonus, 0)), 2) AS known_avg, ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(bonus, 0)), 2) AS overall_avg FROM employees;

title: Fix the average
prompt: This should show the average product price rounded to 2 decimals as average_price, but it fails. Fix it.
starterSql:
SELECT AVG(ROUND(price, 2) AS average_price
FROM products;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS average_price FROM products;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT AVG(price) AS average_price FROM products;
SELECT ROUND(MAX(price), 2) AS average_price FROM products;

title: Revenue from items
prompt: Assume each order item sold for quantity times 10. Show the total as revenue.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT SUM(quantity * 10) AS revenue FROM order_items;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT SUM(quantity) AS revenue FROM order_items;
SELECT COUNT(quantity * 10) AS revenue FROM order_items;

title: Oslo summary
prompt: For Oslo readings only, show the number of readings as days, the average temperature rounded to 1 decimal as avg_temp, and the total rainfall as total_rain.
solutions: SELECT COUNT(*) AS days, ROUND(AVG(temp_c), 1) AS avg_temp, SUM(rainfall_mm) AS total_rain FROM readings WHERE city = 'Oslo';

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS days, ROUND(AVG(temp_c), 1) AS avg_temp, SUM(rainfall_mm) AS total_rain FROM readings;
SELECT COUNT(rainfall_mm) AS days, ROUND(AVG(temp_c), 1) AS avg_temp, SUM(rainfall_mm) AS total_rain FROM readings WHERE city = 'Oslo';
wrongSolutions.why: Skips a day with missing rain
